source_title: IHCL, Adani Airports announce agreement for eight hotels with over 2K rooms
source_excerpt: Indian Hotels Company Limited (IHCL) and Adani Airport Holdings Limited (AAHL) on Thursday announced a multi-hotel operating agreement for eight airport-linked hotels comprising over 2,000 rooms across key locations, including Mumbai, Ahmedabad, Lucknow, and Guwahati. While IHCL is India’s largest hospitality player by market capitalisation, AAHL is the country’s largest airport operator. The hotels will operate under IHCL’s Taj, Vivanta, Gateway, and Ginger brands—comprising three Taj hotels, two Vivanta hotels, one Gateway hotel, and two Ginger hotels—catering to luxury, upscale, and midscale hospitality segments. According to the agreement, development of the hotels would be done by AAHL, and the properties would be operated by IHCL under its multi-brand hospitality portfolio across key aviation gateways. People aware of the details said that construction had begun for Mumbai, Lucknow, and Ahmedabad hotels, with a timeline to operationalise most of the hotels in three to four years. Puneet Chhatwal, managing director and chief executive officer (MD & CEO) of IHCL, said: “As India strengthens its position as one of the world’s fastest-growing aviation markets, airport-centric developments are emerging as important commercial and hospitality hubs.” He added: “Strengthening IHCL’s leading multi-brand presence in India’s key airports, this collaboration will include three Taj hotels, two Vivanta hotels, a Gateway hotel, and two Ginger hotels, catering to the diverse needs of business and leisure travellers across segments. With these additions, IHCL will have 25 hotels across its brandscape at key airports in India.” AAHL has formed Adani Airport City Limited, with the larger aim of developing a land bank of over 655 acres across six airports in five places: Mumbai (including Navi Mumbai), Ahmedabad, Lucknow, Jaipur, and Guwahati. In the first phase, AAHL will invest over ₹20,000 crore to develop about 22 million square feet (msf) across these places. “Across the world, leading airports are evolving into integrated destinations that serve as catalysts for commerce, tourism, and urban growth,” said Jeet Adani, director, AAHL. “Together, we aim to strengthen the hospitality ecosystem within our Airport City developments and contribute to the long-term economic growth of the regions we serve,” he added. In Mumbai, the portfolio will comprise a Taj hotel under construction at Terminal 2 of the airport. In Lucknow, the development will comprise a Vivanta and a Ginger hotel. Ahmedabad will have a Taj and a Vivanta—both in advanced stages of construction—while Guwahati is set to feature a Taj, a Gateway, and a Ginger. These eight properties together will have over 2,000 rooms, featuring a comprehensive mix of accommodation, dining, meetings and events, wellness, and recreational facilities. As passenger traffic, tourism, and business travel continue to strengthen the role of airport-linked districts, this partnership is expected to expand the hospitality infrastructure supporting these key gateways. AAHL has also partnered with IHG Hotels and Resorts earlier this year for five hotels with 1,200 rooms. These hotels will come up in Jaipur, Mangaluru, Thiruvananthapuram, and the Mumbai Metropolitan Region.
